0.long_answer: Fibromyalgia is predominantly associated with alterations in the central nervous system (CNS), which includes the brain and spinal cord. In central sensitization, the CNS becomes hyperexcitable, leading to an amplification of pain signals. This heightened sensitivity results in symptoms like allodynia (pain from normally non-painful stimuli) and hyperalgesia (increased pain from painful stimuli), both of which are commonly observed in fibromyalgia.
